d: Cameron Petersen led 17 laps and held off his teammate Jake Gagne by .438 of a second after Cameron Beaubier crashed out of the lead on lap four while pulling away to what looked like certain victory. Josh Herrin was third.

Cameron Beaubier dominated his comeback ride on Sunday, winning by 3.099 seconds after Jake Gagne suffered with arm-pump issues that left the three-time champion frustrated and out of the points lead. Sean Dylan Kelly was second.

Cameron Beaubier swept both Sunday races with a second dominant performance, winning by 4.648 seconds while Cameron Petersen crashed out of second and remounted before being forced to retire with a broken foot peg. Bobby Fong was second.

Hayden Gillim survived a huge moment at the final corner to pass Jayson Uribe on the last lap and win by .026 seconds in an extraordinary battle. Benjamin Smith was third, with Gillim extending his championship lead to 12 points heading into Sunday.

Hayden Gillim clinched his second straight Stock 1000 Championship with a dominant race win, making history by giving Honda its first-ever MotoAmerica title. Ashton Yates challenged all race but finished second, with Jayson Uribe third.

Rocco Landers controlled the race from the front, holding off a determined Troy Herfoss by just .182 seconds to win his second race of the year. Herfoss' result flipped the championship lead by two points over Kyle Wyman heading into Sunday's finale.

Troy Herfoss dominated Sunday's title decider, passing Kyle Wyman early and never looking back to clinch the 2024 Baggers Championship by 11 points. Rocco Landers charged to second by .119 seconds over a disappointed Wyman in third.
Xavi Fores won his third straight Supersport race in succession at the double-points extended race at Barber. Stefano Mesa was second with Anthony Mazziotto earning his second career podium in third.
